title: 🚗 We're making a story-driven hitchhiking sim where your only way forward is getting into strangers' cars. We're experimenting with AI tools, and we'd love your opinion
author: john_calmer
selftext:
Hey everyone! 😃

We're making **Hitch Happens**, a story-driven hitchhiking sim about weird drivers and road trips that never go to plan.

You stick out your thumb, hop in, and hope your driver is at least somewhat normal. (*Spoiler: not really*.)

You're basically a passenger with a big mouth and way too much curiosity. You decide what to say, which favors to agree to, and how long your driver will put up with you digging through their glove box. Hop out, catch another ride, and the whole story goes somewhere else. Oh, and if a driver ever says "Don't freak out, but...", that's your cue to ask them to pull over.

**How we're using AI to develop Hitch Happens**

AI has been part of almost every stage of development, from artwork and visual assets to coding and prototyping. Since the game mixes 2D and 3D, our main challenge is keeping everything in one consistent style.

Character sprites start in Stable Diffusion: we generate base images and refine them by hand. Gemini and ChatGPT help with precise fixes, like anatomy, poses and clothing details, and MiniMax brings static characters to life with animations we then polish for the game. To make flat sprites sit better in a 3D world, we also create normal, height and roughness maps for them.

We're still experimenting with different tools and workflows, and a few things are still tricky: matching 2D sprites to a 3D world, adding depth with normal maps, and keeping animations consistent. If you've dealt with any of this, we'd love to hear what you tried!
